2. The short facts, giving rise to the issuance of this Rule, are that the plaintiff opposite party Nos.1-5 instituted the above suit against the petitioners and other opposite party Nos. 6-18, for permanent injunction restraining the petitioners from entering into the lands described in the schedule of the plaint. The plaintiffs'' case is that, the suit lands originally belonged to Bhawal Courts of Wards Estate as Khas Khamar and the same were recorded as such in the Khatians of the said Estate during CS Operation. The plaintiffs thereafter took settlement of the suit lands from the aforesaid Estate by two Amalnama dated 4-5-49; that on payment of a salami they were granted rent receipts and since then the plaintiffs have been possessing the land peacefully and adversely to all. It is further stated that the record was duly prepared in the name of the plaintiffs in the SA and RS Khatian on the basis of title and possession. But against the said record of right the principal defendants filed an objection under section 30 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the objection was allowed. Against the said order allowing objection the plaintiffs preferred appeal under section 31 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the appellate revenue officer set aside the order and passed an order for recording the suit land in the names of the plaintiffs. After the order of the appellate officer the plaintiffs started paying rent to the defendant No.1 Government and obtained rent receipts. It is further stated that the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land by constructing dwelling huts, cultivating the land, growing seasonal crops and planting various fruit bearing trees. The lands have been classified as Chala Bari, pond and sail, etc. The plaintiffs alleged that the defendants gave out threat to dispossess them from the suit land and hence the suit. 

 3. The defendants-petitioners contested the said suit by filing written statement, and denied all the materials allegations made in the plaint, that their case is that the suit plot Nos. 1662, 1600, 1596, 1606 1350 and 1410 mouza Anisha Parasad along with other land were declared protected forest by the Gazette Notification No.14177, dated 17-7-1937 and since then the suit plots were in peaceful possession of the Forest Department and they also planted various valuable trees therein. It was further contended that Government decided to constitute reserve Forest relating to the suit plots along with other plots by Notification No. 3125 dated 13-4-1955 and the Collector of Dhaka was appointed as Forest Officer for the purpose. Thereafter objections from the interested quarter (person) were invited in that notification within 90 days but none raised objection as they had no right, title and possession over the suit land. It is further contended that subsequently, the Forest Department by its memo No. 3735(2)/8-12 dated 15-9-67 requested the Government to declare the suit plots along with other plots as reserved forest and it was under the active consideration of the Government. The suit land has been correctly recorded in the name of the defendants and the Forest Department is in peaceful possession. The plaintiffs have created some false deeds to grab the valuable lands and they (plaintiff) have no right, title, and interest in the suit land, so their suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 11. Mr Khondaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite parties, has filed counter affidavit to oppose the Rule. Repelling the above submissions of the learned Attorney-General it is contended by Mr Mahbubuddin Ahmed that the opposite parties had already acquired title in the suit land because of the facts that the suit land originally belonged to Bhawal Courts of Wards Estate as their Khas Khamar land and the plaintiffs along with others took settlement of the suit land from the said Estate by Amalnama on payment of salami on 4-5-49 and they were granted rent receipts by the said Estate. It has been further submitted that suit lands were subsequently recorded in the name of the plaintiffs and they (opposite party) paid rent to the government. Mr Mahbubuddin. Ahmed therefore contends that both the courts below having rightly considered the oral and documentary evidences found plaintiffs'' possession in the suit lands and prima facie title in their favour quite legally. It is therefore urged before me that in a suit for permanent injunction, the question of title is not that material to be looked into but incidentally the court can look into it. 

 14. Mr Khondaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed has contended that CS operation in the locality was completed before 1916 that is, more than 80 years from today and by this time radical changes have taken place in the nature and character of the suit land itself and also the mode of possession thereof by human beings of the locality and it is argued by him that it will be unreasonable to say that the Government officials are so foolish to rely on 80 years old exhibits D and D(1) to agitate that the suit lands still remained as Gazate Garh (that is, till today) is more than unusual. Mr Khandaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed having referred to the statement made in the counter affidavit pointed out emphatically that the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 from his share transferred 4 acres of land out of suit plot No. 1662 to one Towhid Trust in 1995 and the said trust is very much in possession of the part of the suit lands. Besides, the opposite party Nos. 1, 2, and 3 also transferred lands from their shares of plot Nos. 1596, 1600, 1606 and 1662 to some Government servants, journalists and debtors and those transferees are in peaceful possession of their purchased lands and have erected walls, constructed buildings and dug ponds in their plots. Furthermore the opposite party No. 2 donated a portion of lands from his share in plot No. 1596 for a High School in 1989, rest of the same plot and other 5 plots as detailed as schedule A and B to the plaint are in possession of the plaintiffs-opposite parties and successors-in-interest of opposite parties 3-4 who have in the meantime died and their heirs have been substituted as opposite parties Nos. 3-12. 

 21. On scrutiny of the records of the case and upon perusal of the judgments of the courts below, I find that both the courts below discussed the basic documents of prima facie title of the plaintiffs namely, the two Amalnamas the Exts. 1, 1-A(i.e. settlement taken by the plaintiffs from the Bhawal Court's of Ward Estate) that two rent receipt Exts. 2 and 2 A two khatians Exhibits 3 and 3(a) standing in the names of the plaintiffs and preformat defendants. It further appears that during RS operation, the suit lands have been recorded in the names of the plaintiffs and preformat defendants and the plaintiff filed three rent receipts Ext. 5, 5(a) and 5(b) to show their payment of rent for the suit lands for year 1379 to 1382 BS. It further appears that during RS operation the lands were recorded wrongly in the name of the government and against that initial record the plaintiffs preferred appeals and their appeals were allowed vide Ext.6. The trial Court also considered the notifications of the government Ext. A. A(1) and A(2) and other documentary evidence namely Ext. B, C, D and D(1) in their proper perspective.
